confirmed.description: Keshavrao's wrist irons break the chapter rig. His arms are flung wide, one hand on the barrel at far right and the other wrist held by Nagoji at left, with no chain between his cuffs. The script and the bible fix the wrist manacles to a short slack chain about a forearm long. The beat also calls for Nagoji's own wrist chain to clang against Keshavrao's cuffs, and that does not happen.
confirmed.evidence: Crop of p3.3: Keshavrao's right cuff is on the barrel at the far right edge and his other cuffed wrist is at left under Nagoji's bandaged grip, roughly an arm span apart. No connecting chain is drawn between them.

verdict.reason: Confirmed on page 3, panel 3.3, with one correction. In the full-resolution crop, Keshavrao's right wrist is cuffed just past Nagoji's bandaged grip at centre. You can tell it is his because the hand below the cuff is thin, unbandaged and hanging down. His left wrist is cuffed on the barrel at the far right edge. The two cuffs are about a full arm span apart, and no chain runs between them. The cuff on the barrel has no chain at all. The script fixes the irons for every prisoner for the whole chapter in panel 1.1: "wrist manacles joined by a short slack chain about a forearm long". Panel 1.2 puts both men "in collars and manacles", and the 3.3 beat names Keshavrao's cuffs. Later beats depend on him having that chain: 9.1 has "the slack of the wrist chain letting it reach", and in 9.3 his short wrist chain catches on the rope. Spreading his arms this wide is impossible with that chain, and the pose reads at print size because his arms span about half the panel. So this is a real but localized rig error, and major is the right severity. The correction is to the reviewer's second point: the art does show the clang beat, roughly. The chain from Nagoji's lower-left cuff swings up and runs into Keshavrao's right cuff at the grip point before going on up to Nagoji's collar. The "clang does not happen" part is therefore overstated, though how that chain is rigged is unclear. The fix is to redraw Keshavrao with his wrists close together on a forearm-length chain, for example both hands clutching at the barrel or both forearms caught in Nagoji's grip.

confirmed.description: Four lettering elements are crammed into a short strip and read in a zigzag. Keshavrao's 'Others.' sits right of centre, above the stuck section, with a long tail running back to him. Nagoji's reply 'Quickly.' sits lower at the far left. The eye goes right, then back left, then right again to two captions. The script asked for both balloons at the left, at the start of the move.
confirmed.evidence: In the page-6 crop, 'Others.' sits at about x780-900 / y260-340 (display px), and its tail stops near the lantern, about 190px from Keshavrao's head. 'Quickly.' sits at x390-515 / y340-420, 'Liberty was a generous word.' at x578-855 / y360-420, and 'Yet slack iron...' at x765-1180 / y435-525, covering the beam in front of the three stuck men.

verdict.reason:
I confirmed the layout, but it is minor rather than major. The reviewer's positions are accurate. In panel 6.1, "Others." sits right of centre at the top of the strip (display x780-900, y260-340). Its body is closer to the first stuck man's head than to Keshavrao. Its tail points left and ends past the lantern, about 150 original px (about 110 display px) short of Keshavrao's face. "Quickly." sits lower at the far left, next to Nagoji. The two captions then step right and down. This goes against the script's direct note for 6.1: "Letter the two balloons at the left, at the start of the move." So the script does not allow it, and the art shows it.

Why it is not major: the reading order still works. "Others." is clearly the highest element (its top sits about a quarter of the panel height above "Quickly."), so the top-first rule puts it first, which is the correct dialogue order. Its tail points straight at Keshavrao's head, so the speaker is not wrong. All four elements are readable at print size (checked at reduced scale). The cost is a back-and-forth eye path and a slight chance of reading "Quickly." first. With two one-word lines, reading them in reverse barely changes the meaning.

A related polish point: the "Yet slack iron..." caption covers the stuck men's hands and the beam in front of them. Their staring faces and one ring to the left of the caption stay visible, so the "will not give" beat comes through but is weaker. Suggested fix: move "Others." to the left, beside Keshavrao, above "Quickly.", with a short tail.

confirmed.description: The art tells a different story from the script. The script asks for a broadside wave throwing the hold sideways, with men almost weightless for a heartbeat and pen chains snapping sideways. The panel instead shows a long, galley-like central aisle with water running down it. Rows of mostly bare-chested men lean forward and back in unison, so they read as oarsmen rowing, not prisoners being thrown. Nothing is tilted or airborne, and the pen and bench layout does not match the hold set up in 1.1 and 2.1.
confirmed.evidence: Crop of p3 top strip: men seated in long rows on both sides of a flooded aisle, arms forward in a rowing posture, many shirtless rather than in the grey, brown and off-white rags of 1.1. The one sideways force shown is water flowing along the aisle.

verdict.reason: Confirmed at 300 DPI on page 3, panel 3.1 (crop x310-1530, y355-785). The panel shows a long central channel of fast-flowing water running away from the viewer between two straight rows of wooden boxes. In each row, shirtless men in loincloths lean forward together with their arms reaching out, like oarsmen on a galley bench. Nothing is tilted. No body is airborne or thrown sideways. The only sideways force is water running along the aisle, not water surging across the floor to the knee. The script asks for a broadside wave that throws the hold sideways, with men almost weightless for a moment and pen chains snapping sideways. None of that is drawn. The panel also breaks continuity with 1.1 and 2.1. Those panels show a low, dark hold with plank shelves split into pens of four or five clothed men in grey, brown and off-white rags, cross-legged, with the ladder and barrels nearby. Here it is a long, high, colonnaded hall with nearly every man bare-chested. The panel is also rendered in a photoreal, golden-lit film style, unlike the painted look of the panels around it, which makes it read even more like a different place. One point in its favour: the collar-to-collar pen chains run level, never vertical, which matches the chain rig. The flooding still loosely supports the caption about the storm building. So the beat is mostly wrong rather than entirely missing, and the problem is confined to one panel. It still needs a redraw: as drawn it reads as galley slaves rowing, not prisoners being thrown by a wave. Major is the right severity.

refuted.description: Keshavrao's half-page close-up is off his lock. He has a clear dark tuft of hair under the lower lip, and lined, pitted skin that makes him look mid-to-late twenties. The lock and the 07-keshavrao-v15c sheet call for about nineteen, a softer, rounder face, beardless apart from a faint moustache. This is his biggest face in the chapter and the emotional 'ghost of a smile' beat.
refuted.reason: The approved sheet shows the same features the reviewer flagged. I zoomed into the sheet's FAINT MOUSTACHE detail (07-keshavrao-v15c.png, details row). It has a small wispy tuft under the lower lip, in the same place and at the same density as the one in panel 4.2. The sheet's moustache is also about as thick as the panel's, so the claim that the tuft and the fuller moustache are absent from the sheet is wrong. The sheet's NEUTRAL and HAPPY heads also have spotted, pitted skin and faint forehead lines, which match the wet, freckled skin in the panel. The rest of the lock holds: short ragged hair, thin moustache, the grey-brown tunic, the iron collar and no ear stud. The face reads as a young man around twenty, not mid-to-late twenties. I also shrank the panel to roughly print size (about 2.5 inches wide). At that size the tuft is a faint shadow under the lip and does not change who he is or the 'ghost of a smile' beat. The panel is consistent with the sheet, so nothing needs fixing.

refuted.description: Both faces are cropped off by the top frame line. Nagoji is cut just above the moustache, so his eyes and nose are gone and only moustache, chin and ear stud show. Keshavrao's crown is also cut. The script's beat is that both men look up into the open space above their heads. The crop removes that space and removes Nagoji's face, so the reader is left to identify him by hair and tunic alone.
refuted.reason: I zoomed in on the top border of page 5, panel 5 at full 300 DPI. Crops: Nagoji at x 300-600, Keshavrao at x 1250-1550, y 2020-2180. The art doesn't match the report. Nagoji's head is tilted back. The frame line only clips his forehead and crown. Both eyes, his nose, the open mouth, the full moustache, the ear stud and his long curly hair are all clearly inside the panel, and his upward gaze reads plainly. Keshavrao's face is fully visible: brows, eyes, nose and moustache. His spiky hair sits just under the border, with at most the very tips touching it. Both men are clearly looking up, which is the script's beat ("both look up into open space above their heads"). The empty space above them isn't drawn in this panel, but the beat still lands. Each keeps his empty collar, his wrists are manacled, and the chain slides into the water between them, all as scripted. Both are easy to identify by face, not just by hair and tunic. The tight head crop is a stylistic choice and wouldn't be a problem at print size.

refuted.description: The setting changes inside the page. In 7.1 and 7.2 the hatch has a narrow plank-runged ladder, which Nagoji climbs and the guard falls through. In 7.3, captioned 'The ladder was clear.', the camera looks down a broad staircase with deep treads and side stringers. The caption names a ladder over a staircase, and the guard's fall no longer matches the structure.
refuted.reason: On close crops, 7.1 and 7.2 do not show a narrow rung ladder. They show a steep ship's ladder: flat plank treads set between two heavy side rails, with no risers. Seen from straight above, 7.3 shows the same thing: flat plank treads between two side rails, going down into the flooded hold. The treads look deeper and wider in 7.3 only because of the top-down angle. The camera sits at the top of the ladder, so the nearest treads are much closer to it than the prisoners are, which makes them look large, and open plank treads seen from above appear to overlap like stair steps. The ladder still reads as about one person wide next to the barrels and bales, and the number of treads matches what 7.1 shows. The caption "The ladder was clear." fits what is drawn, a ship's ladder of the kind the script calls a ladder throughout. The guard's fall also still works: in 7.2 he drops between the treads, and in 7.3 he lies face-down in the water just past the foot of the ladder, as the script asks. At most the 7.3 treads are a little chunkier than in 7.1, which is too slight to matter at print size. No continuity break.

refuted.description: Pseudo-text is painted into the art. The two gilded carved cartouches on the stern castle rail behind Nagoji hold looping shapes that read as script glyphs, something like a Kannada or Malayalam word, rather than plain scrollwork. That breaks the standing rule against any text in the art. Repaint them as non-glyph foliate carving or plain panels.
refuted.reason: I cropped page-08.png panel 8.1 at native resolution and at 4x and 8x zoom (original pixels about 1180-1300 x 490-560 and 1420-1540 x 510-590). Both stern-castle cartouches hold looping gold strokes inside rectangular frames. Only at 8x do they look a little like curly Indic letterforms. Malayalam's rounded shapes look like almost any looping strapwork, so this resemblance proves little. At native 300 DPI, which is print resolution, each cartouche is about 50 px (roughly 4 mm) wide and the strokes are about 25 px (roughly 2 mm) tall. They sit on a dark, rain-streaked hull behind Nagoji's head. At page scale they read as ordinary carved Baroque scroll panels on a stern castle, which the script asks for ("her carved stern castle rising aft"). I could not spell out any real or clearly glyph-like word, and nothing draws the eye there. The rule against text in the art (CONTINUITY.md line 126) is real, but this is ambiguous ornament and too small to matter at print size. If anyone wants to change it, it is optional minor polish (simplify to foliate carving on the next re-render), not a major defect.

refuted.description: The script marks a page turn after page 7, but with the current folios page 7 and page 8 face each other as one spread. The deck reveal on page 8 is visible while the reader is still on 7.4. The chapter also opens on a left-hand page.
refuted.reason:
Refuted. The reviewer read the folios correctly: page 1 is 16, page 7 is 22, page 8 is 23, page 9 is 24 and page 10 is 25. The conclusion still does not hold, for three reasons.

1. These are not final book folios. /Users/roshanvenugopal/Documents/github/nagoji/output/comic-v15-full-redo/PRODUCTION-PLAN.json says: "Chapter-master folios; final book folios are set at assembly after front matter." Which pages face each other in print is decided at assembly, not by these renders.

2. The pipeline's own layout disagrees with the reviewer's "odd folios are right-hand pages". In pipeline/compositor.py, page_boxes() gives odd folios trim [9,9,441,657] inside a 441 pt media box. That puts the 0.125 in bleed on the left edge, and pipeline/README.md says bleed is on the outside edge. So odd folios are laid out as left-hand pages. On that basis, Ch3 page 1 (folio 16) is a right-hand opener, and page 7 (folio 22) and page 9 (folio 24) are right-hand pages. Both of the script's "*Page turn.*" marks (after 7.4 and after 9.5) then fall on real turns. Under the reviewer's parity, the turn after page 9 would also sit inside a spread, which shows the script was written for a chapter that opens on a right-hand page.

3. Nothing on page 7 shows a defect. 7.4 is staged as the script asks: Nagoji half out of the hatch in rain, empty collar, manacles, bandaged hands, shouting down. The balloon is correct and readable. Page 8 opens on the deck reveal, as scripted. Whether the turn lands inside a spread is an assembly and imposition question, and a redraw of 7.4 would not change it.

At most it is an assembly note, not a page defect: chapter openers should land on a right-hand page, padded with a blank page if needed, and someone should confirm the compositor's odd/even bleed side. Neither is a problem in the 7.4 art or lettering.

refuted.description: The page turn after page 9 also falls inside a spread. 'Keshavrao was gone.' on 9.5 and the leap and sinking on page 10 are visible at the same time, so the last reveal of the chapter loses its turn.
refuted.reason: Refuted. Nothing on the page shows this problem. The claim depends on which side of the spread each page falls, and the files point the other way. (1) In the delivered PDF (chapters/ch03/pdf/Horse-of-the-Servant-V15-Chapter-03-r8.pdf), page 9 (folio 24) has trim box [0,9,432,657], so its 9 pt outside bleed is on the right edge. That makes it a right-hand page. Page 10 (folio 25) has trim [9,9,441,657], with bleed on the left, so it is a left-hand page on the next spread. Page 7 (folio 22) also has its bleed on the right. compositor.py page_boxes gives every even folio its outside edge on the right. By the PDF's own layout, both of the script's '*Page turn.*' marks (after 7.4 and after 9.5) fall on real page turns. The reviewer assumed instead that even folios are left-hand pages. (2) PRODUCTION-PLAN.json says these are 'Chapter-master folios; final book folios are set at assembly after front matter', so the 24/25 numbering is provisional. Final facing pages are not decided at the chapter render stage, and this cannot be pinned on page 9, panel 5. (3) The page itself is fine. 9.5 ends the page with 'Keshavrao was gone.' in the lower-right caption, legible and in the right place for a reveal before the page turn. If anything needs a look, it is the book-wide question of whether the compositor's even-on-the-right convention is intended. That is an assembly question, not a fault on this page.

minors.description: Keshavrao reads older and heavier than his lock. His moustache is thick and droops past the corners of his mouth, his brow is deeply furrowed, and his shoulders and arms are heavily muscled. The lock says about nineteen, clearly smaller and thinner than Nagoji, narrow shoulders, faint moustache. The same bulk shows on page 5 panel 5, with broad pectorals and chest hair, and on page 9 panel 2. In those panels he is close to Nagoji's build.
minors.evidence: Crop of page-09 panel 1 (display 600-720 x 320-420): the moustache is heavy and continues down at the mouth corners. Wider crop: bulky deltoids and biceps on both arms. Page-05 panel 5 crop: chest hair and defined pecs under his open tunic.

minors.description: Nagoji is a little off-model. The ends of his moustache turn down in a chevron instead of the thick curled, upturned ends on the nagoji-v2 sheet. His face is narrower and his hair is centre-parted, so he looks different from his neighbouring panels (3.4, 4.5).
minors.evidence: Crop of page-04 panel 1 (display 330-660 x 400-700): the moustache tips point down at the jaw. The gold stud and clean chin are correct.

minors.description: Nagoji's head is cut through the brow by the top frame line, and the balloon tail runs into his mouth. 'Rounds on them with his teeth bared' is his key expression in this panel, and only the lower half of his face carries it.
minors.evidence: Page-05 panel 3 (display y 630-900): Nagoji at x≈780, head cropped at the eyebrows by the panel top, tail of 'Quiet! You want them to hear?' touching his lips.

minors.description: In the wide shot where Nagoji 'stands small on the deck', the top border cuts his head across the eyes. Only his ear stud, moustache and chin show, which weakens his read in the silent beat where he looks at the empty hatch.
minors.evidence: Crop of page-10 panel 1 (display 330-520 x 255-420): the panel's top rule runs across Nagoji's eye line.

minors.description: Nagoji's ear is visible with no gold stud, though the stud is a constant identity marker. Every other panel in the chapter shows it.
minors.evidence: Zoom of page-07 panel 1 (display 250-330 x 470-540): a bare earlobe in profile under the hair.

minors.description: The ladder and the hold do not match 2.1 on the same page. In 2.1 a steep single-rail ladder stands beside a post with an iron ring, and the prisoner pens sit a few yards from the musket. In 2.4 a broad staircase rises under cascading water and the hold holds only crates and barrels. The musket also changes: 2.1 has a large oval brass buttplate and a full wooden fore-stock, while 2.4 has a plain butt and steel barrel bands.
minors.evidence: 2.1, right: a narrow ladder against a post with an iron ring. 2.4, right: a wide two-stringer stair. 2.4, left: the musket butt has no brass plate.

minors.description: The ladder changes construction within the page. In 6.2 it is heavy squared timber with flat rungs. In 6.4 it has round pole rungs lashed with rope, which is also unlike the plank ladder on page 7.
minors.evidence: 6.2, left edge: flat-rung timber ladder. 6.4, right: round rungs with thick rope lashings at each joint.

minors.description: The musket prop has drifted from its plant on page 2. Here it has a dark steel barrel, two brass barrel bands and a brass band at the wrist of the stock. The 2.1 musket has a full wooden stock and a large brass buttplate.
minors.evidence: 6.3: brass bands at the wrist and fore-end on a dark barrel. Compare the 2.1 foreground musket.

minors.description: The guard's headgear and belt are off the chapter guard look. He wears a round kettle-hat with a drooping brim rather than a steel morion with an upturned brim and crest, the helmet 2.2, 6.5 and 7.1 draw. He also has a wide buckled waist belt under the cross-belt, which the script excludes so that no guard reads as João. The same wide belt reappears on the guard in 7.1.
minors.evidence: 1.4 zoom: a domed hat with a downturned brim, no crest, and a broad waist belt with a buckle. The 7.1 guard has the same broad waist belt.

minors.description: The irons rig is inconsistent. A chain hangs straight down from the front of Nagoji's collar to his wrist chain, which is not part of the rig: the pen chain should run collar to collar through a side ring. Across the chapter the collar ring drifts from the front (1.1, 1.2, 2.1, 6.1, 8.1, 9.4, 10.1, 10.3) to the side (10.2, 10.5).
minors.evidence: 1.1: a vertical chain from the front ring of Nagoji's collar down to his lap. 4.5 shows a similar collar-to-wrist chain. 10.2 and 10.5 show the ring at the side of the neck.

minors.description: The script calls for a broken ladder in the empty hatch, but the ladder is drawn intact. That weakens the story logic that no one else is coming up.
minors.evidence: 10.1, right of centre: a whole ladder stands in the hatch under the cascade.

minors.description: Nagoji's costume drifts. The torn ochre sleeveless tunic is drawn as a shawl or cloak that covers his near shoulder and upper arm, with a long tattered drape behind him. It no longer reads as the captivity-sheet tunic.

minors.evidence: Nagoji's moustache and lower face are visible at display x110-170, y955-1000, cut by the top and left borders of the panel.

minors.description: The top of the first balloon runs into the panel's top border, so the balloon outline and the frame line merge.
minors.evidence: The top of the balloon 'Storms break ships...' is at about display y1067, and the panel's top border is at about y1065.

minors.description: Nagoji's snarl at the prisoners is the beat, but his head is cropped by the panel's top border and pinned under the balloon. The top of his head and his hair are cut off, so the bared teeth sit right at the frame edge.
minors.evidence: p5 panel 3 (displayed y≈625 to 898): Nagoji's face starts at the top border at x≈700, with no headroom, and the 'Quiet! You want them to hear?' balloon is jammed against it.

minors.description: The script asks for the chain hauled level toward the camera with heels braced against the pen plank. Here the chain climbs steeply to the overhead ring and no plank is shown. The panel also drops the water entirely: 5.3 and 5.5 show the hold waist-deep, but here both men stand with dry legs down to the knee.
minors.evidence: p5 panel 4: the chain runs from their fists diagonally up to the splintered ring at the upper right. The lower legs and dhotis are clear of any water line, while 5.5, directly below, shows both men waist-deep.

minors.description: The script has both men working along the beam, yanking rings and kicking wood, with the two balloons lettered at the left at the start of the move. Keshavrao instead sits passively on the beam, legs crossed, holding a chain. His 'Others.' balloon sits at the centre above the staring prisoners, and its tail stops well short of him, so it can read as one of the prisoners speaking.
minors.evidence: p6 panel 1: Keshavrao is seated at x≈560. The 'Others.' balloon is at x≈790 to 900, its tail tip ending at about x≈705, next to the lantern and over the three chained men on the right.

minors.description: The script specifies a side-on, distant shot with both men small on the ladder, to keep the violence at arm's length. The render is a close, large-figure composition with Nagoji at the ladder's foot, one foot in the water. In 7.2 he is suddenly high on the ladder near the hatch, so his position jumps between the two panels.
minors.evidence: p7 panel 1: both figures fill most of the panel height, and Nagoji's left foot touches the flood water at the ladder base. In p7 panel 2 he clings near the top of a tall ladder.

minors.description: The caption 'The ladder was clear.' sits over a broad staircase with flat treads. The ladder Nagoji has just fought on in 7.1 and 7.2 is a narrow rung ladder, and 6.4 drew a rope-lashed pole ladder. The hatch access changes form across the chapter: staircase in 2.1, 2.4 and 7.3; rung ladder in 6.2, 7.1, 7.2 and 10.1.
minors.evidence: p7 panel 3: the bottom of the frame shows wide plank stair treads with side stringers. p7 panels 1 and 2 show a two-stile rung ladder, and p6 panel 4 shows round rungs lashed with rope.

minors.description: The opening beat of the storm arriving 'through the hull' is not drawn. The script asks for near darkness, the whole image tilted hard, bodies sliding against one another and pen chains jerking sideways. The render is a level, warmly lantern-lit hold with prisoners slumped asleep and chains hanging still, so only the captions carry the motion.
minors.evidence: p1 panel 1: horizontal composition with no tilt, bright lantern at the top, neighbouring prisoners asleep with heads bowed, and chains in calm drooping loops.

minors.description: The script calls for jagged, overlapping shout balloons from off panel above. Both sailor balloons are lettered as smooth, rounded, separate speech balloons, so the shouted storm orders read as calm speech.
minors.evidence: p1 panel 3: 'Reef the sails! Haul, haul!' and 'Tie that down! Move, you son of a dog!' sit in smooth oval balloons side by side with no overlap, their tails pointing up.

minors.description: The script tags both of Nagoji's orders as spoken in Marathi, and the adaptation notes say this marks the moment he speaks for all the prisoners. The lettering gives no sign of it: no angle brackets and no translation note.
minors.evidence: p3 panel 2: 'Hold to the beams! Hook your arms over the wood.' and 'Do not let the chain drag you.' are lettered in plain balloons identical to his English dialogue elsewhere. The script snapshot has the speaker as 'NAGOJI (in Marathi)'.

minors.description: Ragged page layout. Panels 3.1, 3.2, 3.3 and 3.5 are set narrower than the art column and indented, while 3.4 runs the full width, leaving uneven side margins. 3.1 is scripted as 'Wide' but renders as one of the narrower panels.
minors.evidence: p3: panels 1 to 3 and 5 span about x 227 to 1098 (displayed), panel 4 spans x 107 to 1217.

minors.description: The script asks for the first sailor balloon before the impact (upper left) and the second after it (lower right), so the order brackets the crash. Both balloons sit along the bottom at about the same height, and the right one's top is slightly higher. The mainmast and pump lines read as simultaneous, and the second may be read first.
minors.evidence: p4 panel 4: 'The mainmast! Cut the rope...' at lower left (top at y≈1560) and 'She is taking water!...' at lower right (top at y≈1490).

minors.description: Ragged layout. Panel 8.2 is a small box centred on the page with wide empty margins either side, while 8.1, 8.3 and 8.4 each have different widths. Keshavrao's cry, an emotional beat, shrinks to a thumbnail.
minors.evidence: p8: panel 2 spans about x 333 to 992 (displayed), against panel 1 at x 107 to 1217, panel 3 at x 120 to 1205 and panel 4 at x 135 to 1190.

minors.description: The script places the caption 'For a moment I was nowhere. Only a body in a cold, roaring universe.' inside the upper-left inset of Nagoji's fingers clawed into the rope coil, tying his dissociation to his own body. It is lettered at the top right of the main panel, next to Keshavrao, and the inset carries no text.
minors.evidence: p9 panel 1: the inset is at x≈107 to 443, y≈258 to 440, with no caption. The caption box is at x≈748 to 1155, y≈260 to 352, above Keshavrao's balloon.

minors.description: The script wants only Nagoji's hands at the frame edge holding the rope. The render includes a sliver of his face cut through at the nose, just a moustache and chin in the top-left corner, which is an awkward crop.
minors.evidence: p9 panel 3: top-left corner (displayed x≈107 to 180, y≈955 to 1000) shows half a moustache and the edge of a chin, cut off by the frame.

minors.description: The script has Nagoji looking at the empty hatch and a broken ladder. In the render he looks down at his own palms, the ladder in the hatch is intact, and the top of his head is clipped by the panel border.
minors.evidence: p10 panel 1: Nagoji's head is tilted down toward his open hands, with his hair cut by the top frame line. The ladder at the right inside the hatch shows whole stiles and rungs.
